notes.title: Approved diagnostic results
notes.text: Approved four-trajectory addendum, separate from the main 27-cell benchmark. All four conditions were executed once, with five judge ratings each. Task133 Late compares an injected omission of allow_variables against the exact correct main Patch snapshot. Task133 Middle compares a historical linked_notes rule against reverting only evaluate.usage_rules. The runtime source matches main commit12d693c; same model, decoding settings, budgets and judge protocol. Missing fact: TF10, PE5.8, 27 calls, 9 errors, output truncated. Complete fact: TF10, PE5.6, 5 calls, 1 error, completed. Rule retained: TF10, PE7.8, 22 calls, 2 errors, truncated. Rule reverted: TF9.8, PE10, 4 calls, no errors, completed. Do not treat five ratings as five executions. Sources: submission/diagnostics-20261031/audit.json and exact-knowledge-diffs.json. Main results remain unchanged.

notes.title: Interpretation and stopping conditions
notes.text: The injected omission directly causes eight missing-parameter rejections, versus zero in the complete snapshot. This confirms a local fault-injection mechanism, not a natural failure of original Selective Patch. Completing the knowledge does not improve PE in this pair:5.6 versus5.8. The complete arm also encounters an upstream missing batch_evaluate handler. Four judge rationales incorrectly call this available tool absent; original ratings remain unchanged. The rule rollback shows fewer calls and higher PE, but TF decreases from10 to9.8. One stochastic execution per arm cannot establish a general causal effect. evaluate is related to the changed validator, so unchanged metadata does not prove an unrelated over-update. Existing six negative rollback diagnostics and all10959 prior evidence files remain intact. All four approved trajectories are terminal; no expansion. Strict natural original-Patch under/over-update gaps remain, and course acceptance of a controlled fault case is not presumed. Sources: diagnostic addendum pages2–3, audit.json, raw trajectories and judge responses.
